To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) analog VLSI provides a useful medium for expressing and testing theories of function; (b) neural structures provide useful architectures for VLSI computation; (c) analog VLSICs are useful tools for exploring and understanding the relationship between form and function in biological systems.

analog VLSIs can be used to understand neural computation, that the idiom of neural computation is a useful idiom for VLSI computation, and that VLSIs provide a new and powerful medium for understanding and expressing neural computation.
analog VLSIs can capture significant portions of neural function and, concomitantly, that incorporating neural architectures can lead to new approaches to computation in analog VLSI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of analog VLSIs as a tool to study the function of neural systems.
the development of a formalism that is appropriate for describing and understanding the function of neural systems.
understanding and expressing the relationship between form and function in neural systems, and the relationship between form, function, and implementation in VLSI analog systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VLSI visual system is a useful tool for studying and understanding visual processing in biological systems.
the relationship between VSLI and neurobiology is not merely a question of mapping, but of the development of a new formal language for the description of computation.
this work is a synthesis of form (neural systems) and function (VLSI systems).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the feasibility of a VLSI analog of a simple visual neural system, and that the resulting chip provides a useful test bed for exploring the relationship between neural function and VLSI implementation.
analog VLSIs are a useful tool for understanding neural computation.
we have developed an analog VLSI visual system, and that the system is a good model of the visual system of a simple vertebrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
analog VLSIs are a powerful medium for expressing neural algorithms and for understanding the function of real neurons and neural structures.
the VLSI medium can be used to capture a significant portion the function of neural systems at the systems level.
VLSI analog circuits are an effective medium of abstraction for expressing the function of neural systems.
